items.X_desc: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Mark yes if it uses explicit explanatory or list framing such as “why,” “how,” “what we know,” or a numbered reason structure.
items.Y_desc: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Headline is phrased as a direct question ("Will this...?", "Why do...?") combined with soft, historical, or scientific subject matter rather than immediate crises.

items.X_desc: Headline poses a question or promises a list using extreme adjectives like most or longest.
items.Y_desc: Headline is formulated as a question (ending with a question mark or starting with interrogatives like why, could, will).

items.X_desc: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Headline names no specific person, country, or institution, relying instead on broad placeholders (e.g., "this place", "celebs", "stars") or abstract references.
items.Y_desc: Headline uses indeterminate verbs like overshadow, quits, or fails rather than concrete actions.

items.X_desc: Mark whether the headline contains quoted speech or a quoted phrase.
items.Y_desc: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: The headline begins directly with a quote expressing helplessness, outrage, or shock, followed by an em-dash identifying the speaker.

items.X_desc: <=8 words | DESCRIPTION: Headline begins with a soft, novelty, or celebrity element, but ends with a tragic, fatal, or violent noun (e.g., "after murder", "after attacks").
items.Y_desc: Headline is formulated as a question (ending with a question mark or starting with interrogatives like why, could, will).

items.X_desc: Headline relies on procedural political verbs like quits, votes out, or congratulates, lacking immediate crisis.
items.Y_desc: Headline relies entirely on an article followed by a dramatic adjective (e.g., 'sabotaged', 'offensive').

anchors.X_name: Presence of a trailing signature block
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for how fully the text ends with a personal sign-off: a name, initials, a handle, or a closing salutation. Extent only.
anchors.Y_name: Author sign-off at the end of the text
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for whether the writer closes by naming or initialling themselves. Extent only; do not judge quality.

anchors.X_name: How much displayed mathematics the text contains
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the density of set-off equation blocks. Count only; do not judge whether the mathematics is correct.
anchors.Y_name: How much the text hedges its own claims
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the frequency of 'I think', 'perhaps', 'it seems' and similar. Count only; do not judge whether the hedging is warranted.
